P1.evidence: No setter on this call, so nothing to read back. No frame of any kind was set — the call opens on a connection problem ('I'm all day. I don't know what's going on.') and the prospect immediately takes control: 'Well, here's the deal, which sort of is part of this conversation. So I'm 65.' No expectations, no agreement question, no open question. The rep never recovered the frame and the prospect ran the agenda for the whole call.

P2.evidence: Age was volunteered in the first fifteen seconds, never asked; height and weight were never taken at all despite fat loss being a stated goal. Work was never asked — the two-acre flower farm surfaced by accident at 00:26:37, twenty-six minutes in. The medical picture was entirely volunteered, but the rep did probe it properly once it landed ('So you've still got three to six months of recovery left. Is that like before you get back to full, like, training how you were?'), which earns a partial. Diet was asked directly and well: 'what we do is heavily nutrition based. Are you on, like, a specific [nutrition plan], I imagine?' No injuries or movement limitations, no training week, no results, no sleep, no energy — the prospect volunteered 'I was just worn out' and it was not followed up.

P3.evidence: Not a single goal question was asked. Everything on the record came unprompted: 'I would like to, you know, get back to get rid of this bit of extra adipose tissue that seems to have settled in my stomach' and the sarcopenia point. A 65-year-old on a flower farm in Hawaii, a month away from his own home, post-transplant, is one of the richest 'what does this actually do for you and who else does it impact' conversations in the corpus, and none of it was opened. The time was available — the rep spent roughly eleven minutes on his own travel plans instead.

P4.evidence: No past-attempts work at all. The prospect handed over the structural gap unprompted — kettlebell classes at his gym stopped after COVID and never restarted, taking his structure and coaching with them — and the rep did not pick it up. He also volunteered the exact competence gap the programme sells against ('the swings and that we do in our class, the snatches and that, that I think require more technical training... So that would be where I would need that assistance') at 00:29:00, and the call ended twenty seconds later without it being used.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. The prospect supplied the consequence himself and in clinical terms — sarcopenia, and older patients who are 'oftentimes, institutionalized, and they have an amazingly hard time snapping back from this' — which is as vivid a two-year picture as any prospect in this corpus will offer. The rep did not engage with it.

P6.evidence: No commitment check. Price was quoted at roughly 00:16 with no belief question and no all-in question either before or after. The nearest thing was the prospect's own 'Well, I think you can help me, I don't know, I think' — a soft yes that the rep answered with a hedge ('Well, I think we can, but I want to make... well, I know we can, but I don't know what's in') rather than a commitment question.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted. The rep deliberately declined to take payment on clinical-timing grounds — 'I also don't want you to pay for something that you can't use right now' — even though the prospect had raised payment himself ('So you take credit card, I presume'). Payment, the Trevor booking, the agreement and the welcome sequence were therefore all out of scope by design.

objection_plays.detail: The trigger is explicit and repeated: 'I'm not sure that this program right now' and 'it will be more useful once i get finished with this healing.' No OD move was run — no 'when does it actually become the right time', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'what if all you had to do was show up'. The rep instead agreed with the objection and strengthened it. Scored as a miss against the script, but flagged for the coach as the defensible exception: OD is written for busy-season excuses, and running 'things never slow down' at a man three to six months out from a faecal transplant would have been the wrong move. The script has no carve-out that lets a rep decline on medical grounds without scoring a miss, and it should.

Clinical fit, and the sharpest instance of the known script gap in this batch. The prospect is post-faecal-transplant with an active, clinician-supervised loading protocol keyed to stool consistency. There is no scripted path for this, so the rep improvised — and improvised largely well, deferring the sale and proposing a gym test-week as the gate. Where it broke down: he never asked whether the treating physicians had cleared kettlebell-specific ballistic work as distinct from general weight-bearing exercise, and he still issued specific purchase weights (2x15 lb and 2x24 lb) for immediate unsupervised home use. A scripted clinical-clearance question would have closed both gaps.

notes: Judged as process, this is close to a null call: phases 1 and 3 through 6 were not run at all, and the only checks that landed were the diet question and a partial on the medical probe. The rep let the prospect run the agenda from the first fifteen seconds and then spent roughly eleven of twenty-nine minutes on his own nomad lifestyle, Japan house purchase and tattoos. Judged as a decision, the outcome was right and should be praised — he declined money from a man in active recovery. Coach the two things separately, and do not let the good decision launder the discovery: the prospect handed over his structural gap, his competence gap and his consequence frame unprompted, and every one of them was left on the floor.
